pdf_row.text: Imboden departs | Jul 4; Jul 5 | Jul 4 afternoon | Jul 5

first_delegated.default_label: Jul 4, evening start (wounded train ordered off)

basis.text: Imboden, who gave the order, puts the head of the column in motion about 4 p.m. on July 4 (Battles and Leaders, 1887); Guild (report of 20 July 1863) has the ambulance trains marching on the evening of the 4th, Lee and Pendleton the order and the escort on the 4th. Nothing found puts his departure on July 5.

default.label: Jul 4 afternoon: the head of the column leaves Cashtown about 16:00 (not Imboden himself)

animation.note: The head of the train starts at about 16:00 on July 4. Selectable positions, memoir only: Imboden himself sets out after dusk the same day (P5); the rear starts at dawn on July 5 (P2). The 20:00 Jul 5 departure is not drawn.

positions.label: Jul 4 (the day the trains were ordered off and began to move)

support.quote: The trains, with such of the wounded as could bear removal, were ordered to Williamsport on July 4, part moving through Cashtown and Greencastle, escorted by General Imboden

witness.name: Robert E. Lee
witness.role: General commanding the Army of Northern Virginia, detailed report of January 1864

support.note: Lee: the trains were ordered to Williamsport on July 4, part through Cashtown and Greencastle escorted by Imboden. Dates an order, not the movement.

support.quote: on the evening of the 4th, our ambulance trains [...] up their line of march by two routes

witness.name: Lafayette Guild
witness.role: Surgeon, Medical Director of the Army of Northern Virginia, report of 20 July 1863

support.note: Guild: the ambulance trains took up their line of march on the evening of the 4th.

support.quote: In the defensive measures directed for the 4th, my care was given to the whole line. [...] were detailed to report to General Imboden, at Cashtown, and aid in guarding the main wagon train back to Williamsport

witness.name: William N. Pendleton
witness.role: Brigadier General, chief of artillery of the Army of Northern Virginia, report of 12 September 1863

support.note: Pendleton: among the measures for the 4th, batteries were detailed to report to Imboden at Cashtown. Dates a detail of escort, not the movement of the train.

reason_not_chosen.text: The day only; the default is the same day with its hour: the head of the column about 16:00.

positions.label: Jul 5 (the rear of the column leaves at dawn; the train reaches Williamsport late)

support.quote: It was found from the position of the head of the column west of the moun- tain at dawn of the 5th — the hour at which Young's cavalry and Hart's battery began the ascent of the mountain near Cashtown — that the entire column was seventeen miles long

witness.name: John D. Imboden
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the cavalry brigade charged with the wagon train of wounded at Cashtown

support.note: Imboden: the rear of the column, Young's cavalry and Hart's battery, began the ascent near Cashtown at dawn of the 5th; the column was seventeen miles long when drawn out. This is the tail, not the departure of Imboden or of the head.
support.page_note: printed page read from the running heads of Battles and Leaders vol. 3 (THE CONFEDERATE RETREAT FROM GETTYSBURG 423 and 424 stand in the text)

support.quote: the batteries accompanying General Imboden arrived with the train at Williamsport late on the 5th

witness.name: William N. Pendleton
witness.role: Brigadier General, chief of artillery, report of 12 September 1863

phrases: arrived with the train at Williamsport late on the 5th

support.note: Pendleton: the batteries with Imboden arrived with the train at Williamsport late on the 5th: an arrival, which a 20:00 departure on the 5th cannot match.

reason_not_chosen.text: Jul 5 dates the tail of the column (dawn) and the arrival at Williamsport, not the departure of Imboden or of the head; no source gives a departure on the 5th, 20:00 included.

inference.step: Imboden puts the start of the rear of the column at dawn of the 5th and Pendleton the arrival at Williamsport late on the 5th; the 5th is read as the day the column was still leaving Cashtown, not as the day Imboden departed.

positions.label: Jul 4 afternoon: the head of the column leaves Cashtown about 16:00

support.quote: On the morning of July 4th my written instructions, and a large official envelope addressed to President Davis, were handed to me

witness.name: John D. Imboden
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the cavalry brigade charged with the wagon train of wounded at Cashtown

support.note: Imboden in Battles and Leaders (1887): on the morning of July 4th he received his written instructions. Names the day of the passage that follows.
support.page_note: printed page 422, read from the running heads (423 stands a few lines later)

support.quote: As the afternoon wore on there was no abatement in the storm. [...] About 4 p. M. the head of the column was put in motion near Cashtown, and began the ascent of the mountain in the direction of Chambersburg

witness.name: John D. Imboden
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the cavalry brigade charged with the wagon train of wounded at Cashtown

support.note: Imboden, 24 years later and as the officer in charge: 'About 4 p. M. the head of the column was put in motion near Cashtown, and began the ascent of the mountain in the direction of Chambersburg.' The head of a column 17 miles long, not the whole train and not Imboden himself, who 'remained at Cashtown giving directions'.
support.page_note: printed page read from the running heads of Battles and Leaders vol. 3 (THE CONFEDERATE RETREAT FROM GETTYSBURG 423 and 424 stand in the text)

support.quote: the head of it left the scene of conflict amidst a terrific rain storm about four o'clock in the afternoon of Saturday, July 4th

witness.name: Jacob Hoke
witness.role: Chambersburg author of The Great Invasion (1887), a local history of the campaign (not an eyewitness of the departure)

support.note: Hoke, a Chambersburg writer, in 1887: the head of the train, in Imboden's charge, left in a terrific rain storm about four o'clock in the afternoon of Saturday, July 4th. No source named; the same hour and rain as Imboden's article of the same year, so possibly drawn from it. Counted in Imboden's line of knowledge, not as a second witness.
support.page_note: no printed page marks in the text layer; the passage is in the chapter on the retreat

inference.step: Imboden, who gave the orders, puts the head of the column in motion about 4 p.m. on July 4; a memoir of 1887 documents what he said, not the fact. Hoke repeats the hour with no source named.

positions.label: Jul 4 evening: the ambulance trains take up their march (Guild)

support.quote: on the evening of the 4th, our ambulance trains [...] up their line of march by two routes

witness.name: Lafayette Guild
witness.role: Surgeon, Medical Director of the Army of Northern Virginia (at Gettysburg), report of 20 July 1863

support.note: Guild, medical director, 16 days after: 'on the evening of the 4th, our ambulance trains took up their line of march by two routes ... One train went by Cashtown, the other by Fairfield.' He does not name Imboden and gives no hour.

support.quote: The trains, with such of the wounded as could bear removal, were ordered to Williamsport on July 4, part moving through Cashtown and Greencastle, escorted by General Imboden

witness.name: Robert E. Lee
witness.role: General commanding the Army of Northern Virginia, detailed report of January 1864

support.note: Lee, six months after: the trains with the wounded were ordered to Williamsport on July 4, part through Cashtown and Greencastle escorted by Imboden. The order and the day, no hour.

reason_not_chosen.text: Guild gives the evening of the 4th for the ambulance trains with no hour; this may be the same start or the trains leaving Gettysburg before the head reached Cashtown.

positions.label: Jul 4, after dark: Imboden himself sets out from Cashtown

support.quote: After dark I set out from Cashtown to gain the head of the column during the night

witness.name: John D. Imboden
witness.role: Brigadier General, commanding the cavalry brigade charged with the wagon train of wounded at Cashtown

support.note: Imboden himself, after the head had gone: 'After dark I set out from Cashtown to gain the head of the column during the night.' Sunset was 19:32 (local mean time); he gives no hour.
support.page_note: printed page read from the running heads of Battles and Leaders vol. 3 (THE CONFEDERATE RETREAT FROM GETTYSBURG 423 and 424 stand in the text)

reason_not_chosen.text: This is Imboden's own departure to catch up with the head of the column, hours after it started.

inference.step: Imboden says the head of the column moved about 4 p.m. and that he himself set out after dark; sunset was at 19:32 and dusk falls after it, so his own start is after about 19:30 on the 4th.

weighing.summary: Every source that dates the departure puts it on July 4: Imboden about 4 p.m. for the head of the column and after dark for himself; Guild the evening of the 4th; Lee and Pendleton the day. Jul 5 dates the tail at dawn and the arrival. Class settled; tier inferred because the hour rests on Imboden's memoir.
weighing.who: Imboden commanded the escort and gave the orders at Cashtown; Guild was the army's medical director at Gettysburg; Lee commanded; Pendleton commanded the artillery that gave the batteries. Hoke is a Chambersburg writer, not a witness of the start.
weighing.when: Guild wrote 16 days, Pendleton 10 weeks and Lee 6 months after; Imboden and Hoke 24 years after. A contemporary report outranks a memoir, but Guild gives a period (evening), not a clock, so the hour comes from the memoir and carries the inferred tier.
weighing.where: Imboden was at Cashtown directing the column on the 4th, and set out after dark; Guild saw the ambulance trains leave Gettysburg and stood at the army's hospitals; Lee, Pendleton and Hoke were not at Cashtown at the hour.
weighing.how_knew: Imboden gives the hour of his own order, with his rain-bound day around it; Guild reports what he saw and ordered; Hoke, no source.
weighing.clock: Confederate clock; the reported difference of about 20 minutes from the Union clock is not applied and is not at issue between these accounts.
weighing.independence: Imboden, Guild, Lee and Pendleton are separate writers, but Lee's report of January 1864 may rely on Pendleton and Guild; only Imboden gives an hour. Hoke may copy Imboden (same hour and rain, same year) and is counted in his line. Two lines (Guild, Lee) give the 4th without an hour; one (Imboden, with Hoke) gives the hour, so the value is single-source.

source_panel_text: Jul 4, about 16:00, from Cashtown: Imboden, who gave the order, says the head of the wagon train started then (1887); Imboden himself left only after dusk, and the rear at dawn on Jul 5. Guild (1863) has the trains marching on the evening of the 4th. No source puts a departure on Jul 5. Three other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: Jul 4 afternoon holds: Imboden puts the head of the column in motion about 4 p.m. The hour rests on a memoir of 1887, so the tier is inferred.

first_delegated.note: Jul 4, evening start holds as the day and as Guild's contemporary wording for the ambulance trains, which gives no hour and may be the same start or the trains leaving Gettysburg; the default is the head at about 16:00, which Imboden gives.

Row 'Jul 4 late afternoon' (Cashtown, Chambersburg Pike; train 15-20 miles; 'Imboden personally leaves about 20:00 per another'): the head leaves about 16:00 Jul 4 and Imboden after dark Jul 4 (his own article); the 'late afternoon of Jul 5' assembly is unsourced. Not edited here.

Row 'Jul 5 ~20:00 NIGHT' (Cashtown; Imboden leaves per one account): no source found for a Jul 5 departure; Pendleton has the train arriving at Williamsport late on the 5th. The row should be dropped or relabelled as the tail of the column (dawn Jul 5). Not edited here.

Row 'Jul 4 01:00 NIGHT' (Lee summons Imboden; 'Imboden's own narrative not retrieved'): Imboden's narrative is now local (BL-3); it has Lee's summons about 11 p.m. on the night of July 3 and a conversation about 1 o'clock. Not read further here; no change to this resolution.
Row 'Jul 4 NIGHT (Guild)' (Cashtown and Fairfield columns): Guild says 'on the evening of the 4th', consistent with the head leaving about 16:00 and the main march by night. No change required.

what_would_change_it: A letter, diary or report of an officer at Cashtown on July 4, or Imboden's own report of the retreat if it exists in the archives, giving an hour with its clock for the start of the column, would test the 16:00 and could raise the tier.
